## Analysis: Was the Claim That Red No. 3's Removal "Was Not Final and Might Never Take Effect" a Fair Reading in Mid-2025?

### The Procedural Context in Mid-2025

The January 2025 order (90 FR 4628) revoked the color additive listings for FD&C Red No. 3 in food (effective January 15, 2027) and ingested drugs (effective January 18, 2028). However, under sections 701(e)(2) and 721(d) of the FD&C Act, the filing of objections **automatically stayed** the effectiveness of the repeal. As the later document confirms:

> "Under sections 701(e)(2) and 721(d) of the FD&C Act, the filing of objections operates to stay automatically the effectiveness of our repeal of §§ 74.303 and 74.1303 until we take final action on the objections." [91 FR 50475 (V. Summary and Conclusions)]

Objections were filed by the February 18, 2025 deadline, which triggered this automatic administrative stay. So in mid-2025, the order was indeed **stayed**—it was not yet in final effect, and the effective dates were suspended pending FDA's resolution of the objections.

### Was It "Fair" to Say It Might Never Take Effect?

**Partially fair, but ultimately misleading:**

- **Fair in a narrow procedural sense:** The order was genuinely stayed. Until FDA ruled on the objections, the repeal was not operative. In theory, if FDA had found the objections meritorious, it could have modified or revoked the order.

- **Misleading as a substantive matter:** The basis for the revocation was the **Delaney Clause**, which operates as a matter of law once the finding of carcinogenicity is made. As FDA stated: "Under the Delaney Clause this finding of carcinogenicity renders the color additive 'unsafe' as a matter of law" [90 FR 4628 (VI. Conclusion)]. FDA explicitly noted it has **no discretion** to retain a listing once the Delaney Clause is triggered: "FDA does not have discretion to list a color additive determined to be safe under the general safety clause if it is found to induce cancer under the Delaney Clause. The Delaney Clause clearly states that such color additive 'shall be deemed unsafe, and shall not be listed'" [91 FR 50475 (B. Objection 2)]. Given this legal framework, the prospect that the order would simply "never take effect" was always remote absent a successful legal challenge to the underlying carcinogenicity finding itself or Congressional action.

### The Position Now

FDA has issued its final action on the objections (91 FR 50475), and the result is unambiguous:

> "We are overruling the objections and denying the requests for a public hearing." [91 FR 50475 (V. Summary and Conclusions)]

> "We are ending the administrative stay of the January 2025 order, and under the January 2025 order we are repealing the listing for FD&C Red No. 3 in § 74.303 as a color additive in food and § 74.1303 as a color additive in ingested drugs effective **January 15, 2027**, and **January 18, 2028**, respectively." [91 FR 50475 (V. Summary and Conclusions)]

The administrative stay has been lifted. The effective dates are confirmed. The revocation is now **final agency action**. Upon those dates, any use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food or ingested drugs will render those products adulterated [90 FR 4628 (VI. Conclusion)].

### Conclusion

In mid-2025, it was accurate to say the order was procedurally stayed and not yet final. However, characterizing it as something that "might never take effect" overstated the uncertainty, given the mandatory, non-discretionary nature of the Delaney Clause. The position now is settled: the ban is final, the stay is lifted, and FD&C Red No. 3 will be removed from food by January 15, 2027, and from ingested drugs by January 18, 2028.

## CFR Provisions Changed by the Red No. 3 Order

The January 2025 order affects two CFR provisions, and they do **not** all change on the same day:

### 1. **§ 74.303** (Use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food, including dietary supplements)
- **Action:** Removed/revoked — the regulation will no longer provide for the safe use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food.
- **Effective date:** January 15, 2027

### 2. **§ 74.1303** (Use of FD&C Red No. 3 in ingested drugs)
- **Action:** Removed/revoked — the regulation will no longer provide for the safe use of FD&C Red No. 3 in ingested drugs.
- **Effective date:** January 18, 2028

### Additional Interim Amendment to § 74.1303
Because § 74.303 is removed first (before § 74.1303), and § 74.1303 previously cross-referenced § 74.303(a)(1) and (b) for identity and specifications, the order also **amends § 74.1303** to incorporate the identity and specifications language directly into that section. This amendment takes effect on the same date § 74.303 is removed (January 15, 2027), so that § 74.1303 remains complete and self-contained during the period between the two removal dates.

### Summary
- The two removals occur on **different dates** — food use ends about a year before ingested drug use.
- The staggered timeline gives manufacturers of ingested drugs additional time to reformulate compared to food manufacturers.
